chapters.title: Chapter 1: Real Estate Through an Investor's Eyes

lessons.title: What Makes Real Estate an Asset Class?

children.text: Ask your parents where their wealth sits. The answer is almost never a stock portfolio. The RBI's Household Finance Committee (2017) found that the average Indian household held 77% of its assets in real estate and only 5% in financial assets. Most Indian families have made one enormous property bet without ever treating it as an investment decision. This lesson fixes that.

body.title: Where the Average Indian Household's Assets Sit (RBI, 2017, %)

body.text: A home is shelter you consume. An investment property is an asset you underwrite. The same flat can be either one. What makes it an investment is judging it on cash flow, cost and exit price instead of emotion.

children.text: What Makes Something an Asset Class

markDefs.definition: A group of investments that share similar return drivers, risks and rules, and so tend to behave alike in different market conditions.
The underlying sources that generate an investment's return, such as business profits, interest payments, rent or price changes.

, risks and rules, and so tend to behave alike. Equity pays you from business profits. Debt pays you contractual interest. Gold pays you nothing and only changes in price. Real estate is a claim on land and buildings. It pays rent and changes in value with location, demand and interest rates.

It is a physical asset, which is a big part of its emotional pull.

markDefs.definition: An asset where every unit is different from every other, so there is no single market price that applies to all of them.

body.text: You can buy one unit of a Nifty 50 ETF for a few hundred rupees on Zerodha and sell it before lunch. A 2BHK in Wakad, Pune costs close to ₹1 crore, takes months to sell, and cannot be sold in halves. That gap in divisibility and liquidity explains most of the difference between the two asset classes.

body.caption: Gross yield ignores costs. Net yield subtracts maintenance, property tax and vacancy first.

children.text: Take a 2BHK in Hinjewadi, Pune, bought for ₹90 lakh and rented at ₹25,000 a month. The gross yield is 3.33%. After maintenance and property tax, the net yield is 2.67%. If prices rise 5% a year, the total return is roughly 7.67% a year, before loan interest, tax, vacancy and the cost of buying.
Annual costs: maintenance ₹4,000 × 12 = ₹48,000, plus property tax ₹12,000, for a total of ₹60,000

body.label: Typical gross rental yield on homes in major Indian cities
body.context: ANAROCK data for early 2026 put yields at about 3.2% in Delhi and about 4.9% in Chennai. Home loan rates are around 7.25% to 8.5%, so rent alone rarely covers the EMI.

body.prompt: A flat in Velachery, Chennai costs ₹80 lakh and rents for ₹28,000 a month. What is its gross rental yield, in %?

body.text: "My uncle's flat tripled in 15 years" sounds spectacular. Run the CAGR and it works out to about 7.6% a year, before stamp duty, brokerage, maintenance, years of vacancy and tax. Always turn property stories into an annual rate before comparing them with anything else.

body.title: The uncle's flat
body.prompt: A flat bought in 2011 for ₹30 lakh sells in 2026 for ₹90 lakh. What is its CAGR, in %? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: (90 ÷ 30)^(1/15) minus 1 = 3^0.0667 minus 1 ≈ 7.6%. That return is respectable, but it is below what the headline "tripled" suggests to most people.

columns.label: Self-occupied home
points: Judged on commute, schools and comfort
Its "return" is the rent you do not pay
You rarely sell, because you still need somewhere to live

columns.label: Investment property
points: Judged on yield, appreciation and tenant demand
Rent is received in cash and taxed under "Income from House Property"
The exit is planned from day one

children.text: This is why counting your own home as an investment is misleading. You cannot sell it to fund retirement without buying or renting another place to live. It is an asset on your balance sheet, but it is not a portfolio holding you can freely use.

body.title: Spot the odd one out
body.question: Which of these is NOT a trait of real estate as an asset class?
options: Every property is different from every other
Its price is discovered on an exchange every second
It can earn both rent and capital appreciation
body.explanation: Physical property has no live exchange price. Values come from negotiated deals, circle rates and portals. Only listed routes like REITs and realty stocks get second-by-second prices.

body.title: Name the trait
body.textWithBlank: Because a flat usually cannot be sold quickly without cutting the price, real estate is described as an ___ asset.
body.explanation: Illiquidity is one of real estate's defining traits. Selling takes time, and a quick sale usually means a lower price.

body.title: Meera's ₹25 lakh
body.scenario: Meera is 32, works in tech in Bengaluru and rents her flat. She has ₹25 lakh saved. A broker is pushing a ₹1.1 crore investment flat in Sarjapur Road, using her savings as the down payment and a home loan for the rest.
body.prompt: Using the traits from this lesson, what questions should Meera answer before deciding?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Concentration: almost all her savings would sit in one asset, in one micro-market.
2. Leverage: an ₹85 lakh loan at around 8% costs about ₹6.8 lakh a year in interest early on. A 3% to 4% rental yield brings in roughly ₹3.3 to 4.4 lakh. The gap comes out of her salary.
3. Transaction costs: stamp duty, registration and other charges take a large bite on day one.
4. Liquidity: would she have an emergency fund left? Could she sell quickly if she lost her job?
5. Time: is she willing to manage tenants and repairs?
6. Alternatives: could REITs or listed realty stocks give her real estate exposure with far less concentration?
7. Clarity of purpose: is this an investment, or a future home? The two are judged differently.

points: Real estate is a distinct asset class: a claim on land and buildings that earns rent and changes in value.
Indian households are heavily overweight property, at about 77% of assets in the RBI's 2017 study.
Its defining traits are physical, unique, location-bound, lumpy, illiquid, costly to trade and easy to borrow against.
Total return = net rental yield + capital appreciation. Gross metro yields of about 3% to 5% are well below home loan rates.
Convert every "it doubled" or "it tripled" story into a CAGR before you compare it.
Your own home is an asset, but not a freely usable investment.
REITs, realty stocks, SM REITs and AIFs offer exposure to real estate without buying a flat.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment advice. Property values, rents and loan rates vary widely by city and project. Consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser before making investment decisions.
